qt: to the Commission Estrella Galán (The Left), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE), Estelle Ceulemans (S&D), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Damien Carême (The Left), Pernando Barrena Arza (The Left), Ville Niinistö (Verts/ALE), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left), Anthony Smith (The Left), Hana Jalloul Muro (S&D), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew), Catarina Martins (The Left), Diana Riba i Giner (Verts/ALE), Elisabeth Grossmann (S&D), Ana Miranda Paz (Verts/ALE), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE) Subject:

On 12 and 13 July 2025, serious racist attacks occurred in Torre Pacheco (Murcia, Spain), targeting homes, businesses, and vehicles linked to migrant communities. These events1 took place in a climate of hate speech, promoted by the political party Vox2, and involving far-right groups, who through social media organised a ‘hunt’ targeting migrants3. In compliance with Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union and Article 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, and considering the withdrawal of the proposed horizontal anti-discrimination directive: 1.

How will the Commission ensure Member States effectively implement and enforce Council Framework Decision 2008/913/JHA to prosecute public incitement to hatred or violence based on racism or xenophobia?

Will the Commission promote horizontal equality legislation to ensure Member States actively combat hate speech, especially when promoted by public officials, including by sanctioning hate speech occurring within EU institutions?

What is the current status of negotiations to include hate crimes and hate speech in the list of ‘Euro crimes’ under Article 83.1 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and what measures does the Commission plan to take to unblock this process in the Council?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.9.2025) The Commission is committed to ensuring that there is no place for hate in the EU1. The Framework Decision 2008/913/JHA on combating racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law2 regulates at EU level the criminal response against hate offences in the EU. It concerns all offenders, including public officials. The Commission monitors the implementation of the Framework Decision, including in Spain. It remains, however, the competence of national authorities to investigate, prosecute, and try in accordance with applicable national legislation individual cases of alleged hate offences. With a view to supporting the implementation of the Framework Decision on the ground, the Commission has in place a comprehensive policy toolbox developed with national authorities, EU agencies and international organisations under the High-Level Group on combating hate speech and hate crime3. As regard the EU institutions, their workplaces and their staff adhere to the highest standards in tackling discrimination and combatting hatred. This is a major priority for the Commission4, reflected in its HR Strategy adopted in 2022 and its Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan5. The possible inclusion of hate speech and hate crime in the list of ‘EU crimes’ under Article 83(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union requires a Council decision adopted at unanimity and with the consent of the European Parliament. To date, the Council has not reached the needed unanimity.
